name: Canberra Times cryptic crossword, Wednesday 12 December 1990 (English cryptic)

clue.text: It means freedom for people in France, this reform

indicators.note: to reform something is to remake it, so the place name and the word after it are rearranged
the people are placed inside the rearranged letters, as the word in says

blocks.note: the two words taken letter for letter as raw material
men are people in the general sense

explanation.surface: A political reform in France that brought liberty to the people.
explanation.walkthrough: The people go inside the reshuffled letters, near the end. This is an old word for liberation, rarer than enfranchisement.
explanation.definitionFit: Franchisement is an archaic noun for the act of setting free, the liberty granted to a person.

clue.text: Giving an answer on the subject of forming a union

blocks.note: re is Latin-derived for concerning, on the subject of
joining things forms a union of them

explanation.surface: Replying to a question about getting married or joining a trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: To rejoin is to reply, especially sharply, so rejoining means making a reply.

clue.text: The more pleasant part of the Napoleonic era

indicators.note: part of means only a portion of the following words is used, a run of letters lying across them

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: Pointing to the better side of Napoleon's time in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicer is the comparative of nice, meaning more pleasant or agreeable.

clue.text: Speed gets the heartless

indicators.note: without a heart means the middle letter of the word is taken out

blocks.note: to have is to get or obtain
taken as written before losing its middle

explanation.surface: A cruel person is the one who wins the race.
explanation.definitionFit: Haste is hurry or quickness of movement, a synonym for speed.

clue.text: Racialist characters can be critical

indicators.note: says the letters of the word before could form something else, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Bigoted people may be quick to find fault.
explanation.definitionFit: Satirical writing mocks and censures its targets, so it is critical in the fault-finding sense.

clue.text: The undertaker guy's retained or back in charge, it appears

indicators.note: back means the following words run backwards
a thing retained is held inside, so the guy holds everything that follows

blocks.note: a guy is a man
taken as written
i/c is the abbreviation for in charge
taken as written

explanation.surface: The funeral director's assistant seems to have kept his job or returned to lead it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' turns round the pair 'in charge, it' together, not just one of them; the guy then retains everything else, split after his first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A mortician is the American term for an undertaker, who prepares the dead and arranges funerals.

clue.text: A quartet in the North-east is not affected

indicators.note: in means placed inside the region named next

blocks.note: NE is the compass abbreviation for north-east
taken as written
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A group of four musicians from northern England remain unpretentious.
explanation.definitionFit: Naive means artless and unsophisticated, so free of affectation or pretence.

clue.text: Set against standard allowance for fire

blocks.note: a con is an argument against, as in pros and cons
a standard is a flag or banner
a ration is a fixed allowance

explanation.surface: Weighing up the usual heating allowance against something else.
explanation.definitionFit: A conflagration is a large, destructive fire, an extreme example of a blaze.

clue.text: He's stylishly original

blocks.note: surface reading: a man with a creative, fashionable flair
setter's reading: someone whose job is creating original styles in clothing

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like praise of a person's character, but describes a profession in fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: A dress designer creates new clothing styles, so originality in style is the job.

clue.text: Takes exception to some articles

blocks.note: first meaning: a verb, protests against
second meaning: a plural noun, things or items

explanation.walkthrough: 'Articles' suggests grammar (a, the) or legal clauses; here it simply means things.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb meaning protests against and a plural noun meaning physical items or things.

clue.text: Dog making blunder brought into line

indicators.note: something brought into another thing ends up inside it, so one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: a tier is a row or line, as of seats
to err is to blunder

explanation.surface: A dog that makes a mistake is brought back to heel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Line' here is a row, as in tiered seating, not a leash.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrier is a breed type of small, lively dog originally bred for hunting vermin.

clue.text: Religious person demanding fair exchange, right?

indicators.note: in an exchange things change places, so the letters of the preceding word swap round

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A churchgoer insists on a fair deal and asks whether that is right.
explanation.definitionFit: A friar is a member of a religious mendicant order, such as a Franciscan or Dominican.

clue.text: Being advanced by a peer in a letter

blocks.note: an earl is a peer of the realm
taken as written
ess is the spelt-out name of the letter S

explanation.surface: Someone gets promoted thanks to a lord's letter of recommendation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a container signal, but here it just supplies its own two letters between the peer and the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Earliness is the state of being ahead of time, so being advanced in time or development.

clue.text: Flying can be scary!

blocks.note: surface reading: air travel is frightening
setter's reading: a word for in flight, which can also be read as inspiring awe

explanation.walkthrough: The answer means on the wing, but split it as awe-ing and it means filling with awe, which is how flying can be scary.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an old adverb meaning in flight, on the wing, as birds are when airborne.

clue.text: The guard ride with anger seething

indicators.note: something seething is churning and boiling, so its letters are thrown about

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A furious sentry rides out on horseback.
explanation.walkthrough: The Grenadier Guards are a British Army regiment, so a grenadier is a guardsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A grenadier is a soldier of the Grenadier Guards, one of the British royal guard regiments.

clue.text: A direction may be noticed to cause split

definitions.note: the answer is a past-tense verb; the definition is the bare verb phrase

indicators.note: 'may be' says the next word could be turned into something else, a loose signal to rework its letters

blocks.note: south-east is a compass direction
taken letter for letter, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A spotted instruction might lead people to part company.
explanation.definitionFit: To section something is to divide it into parts, so the answer means having split it.

clue.text: Assistant hurt pointlessly over a complainer being backed

indicators.note: without a point, meaning one compass point letter is removed from the word before
backed means sent backwards, so the complainer is read in reverse

blocks.note: to suffer is to be hurt
taken as written
a nag is someone who complains persistently

explanation.surface: A helper is injured for no reason by a grumbler who has support.
explanation.walkthrough: E (east) drops out. In a down clue, 'over' places the first part above the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A suffragan is an assistant bishop, appointed to help a diocesan bishop.

clue.text: Wooded area with no elders

blocks.note: straight reading: a well-known woodland region
setter's reading: a forest with no old trees, or elder trees, would be a young one

explanation.walkthrough: The New Forest is a large area of woodland and heath in Hampshire, southern England. Read literally, a forest with no older trees in it would be a new one.
explanation.definitionFit: The New Forest is a famous ancient woodland in southern England, despite its name.

clue.text: In a sorry state

blocks.note: surface reading: in a wretched or dilapidated condition
setter's reading: feeling sorry, full of remorse

explanation.walkthrough: A sorry state usually means a mess, but read literally it is the state of being sorry.
explanation.definitionFit: Regretful means feeling remorse or sorrow, so a regretful person is in a state of being sorry.

clue.text: Small creatures the modern holy man backs

indicators.note: to back is to go backwards, so the holy man's letters run in reverse

blocks.note: modern means new
St is the abbreviation for saint, a holy man

explanation.surface: A present-day priest supports some little animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backs' reads as supports; it is the signal to read the saint backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Newts are small amphibians, so they are an example of small creatures.

clue.text: Its use might well result in words being exchanged!

definitions.text: Its use might well result in words being exchanged!

blocks.note: surface reading: an argument, people trading angry words
setter's reading: a reference book you consult to swap one word for another of the same meaning

explanation.walkthrough: Having words means quarrelling, but this book helps a writer replace one word with a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesaurus lists synonyms, so a writer uses it to substitute one word for another.

clue.text: Sheep pounds in Surrey

definitions.note: short for a place in Surrey

blocks.note: a ewe is a female sheep
L is the abbreviation for a pound, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Livestock pens in the English county of Surrey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pounds' looks like animal pens, fitting the sheep, but it is money. Surrey is a county just south of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Ewell is a town in Surrey, England, near Epsom, so it is a place in that county.

clue.text: Finding a sailor in the way, show surprise

indicators.note: in means placed inside the next word

blocks.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: Someone is startled to find a seaman blocking their path.
explanation.definitionFit: To start is to jump or flinch suddenly, a physical sign of surprise.

clue.text: A wish to be in company

blocks.note: taken as written
to long is to wish or yearn

explanation.surface: Someone hopes to join a firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Company' suggests a business; here 'in company' means accompanying someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Along can mean with someone as a companion, as in 'bring a friend along'.

clue.text: Very musical, but needs craft in a first class situation

definitions.note: the answer is a musical direction meaning very

indicators.note: in places the craft inside the phrase that follows

blocks.note: taken as written
SS is the abbreviation for steamship, a craft
A1 means first class, with the 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: Someone very talented in music still needs skill to reach the top rank.
explanation.walkthrough: The ship goes between 'a' and A1. 'Craft' suggests skill, but it is a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Assai is an Italian musical direction meaning very, as in allegro assai, very fast.

clue.text: There's no prison in Gateshead for 22 down

definitions.note: the cross-reference stands for the answer to 22 down, a noun meaning a beginning

blocks.note: an open prison has no locked cells, so open stands for not shut in
taken as written
split as Gates head: the head, or first letter, of Gates

explanation.surface: Gateshead, a town in north-east England, apparently has no jail.
explanation.walkthrough: Gateshead is split into Gates and head, which takes its first letter. 22 down is START, and an opening is a start.
explanation.definitionFit: An opening is a beginning, the same as a start, as in the opening of a play.

clue.text: Cold continent

blocks.note: first meaning: stern and unfriendly in manner
second meaning: as an adjective, self-restrained and abstinent

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cold continent' calls up Antarctica, but continent is the adjective meaning self-controlled.
explanation.definitionFit: Austere describes a severe, unwarm manner and also a self-denying, abstemious way of living.

clue.text: Music men insist clatter is essential

indicators.note: a loose signal: what is essential to the two words is their letters, which are reorganised

blocks.note: the two words taken letter for letter, thirteen in all

explanation.surface: Some musicians claim that noise is a vital part of their art.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is exactly the thirteen letters of 'insist clatter'; the signal for rearranging them is weak, with 'is essential' the only words left over.
explanation.definitionFit: Clarinettists are players of the clarinet, so they are musicians, here called music men.
